text:
Diamondback to Buy Double Eagle’s Midland Stake for $5 Billion

What I Cover My focus spans the global energy landscape and the technologies reshaping it, specifically focusing on oil and gas, renewables, and tech-driven market…

Diamondback Energy agreed on Monday to buy Double Eagle’s 40% share of their Midland Basin partnership for cash and stock that Reuters valued at about $5.03 billion, a purchase that gives it a bigger share of wells it had already planned to drill without adding a rig.

Diamondback formed the partnership in 2022, pairing its subsurface knowledge of the Midland Basin’s emerging Barnett zone with Double Eagle’s land expertise, Chief Executive Kaes Van’t Hof said. He called the buyout the culmination of that partnership, and said Diamondback’s confidence in the resource and in its own costs made this the time to complete it.

Diamondback’s first full-section Barnett development, four 10,000-foot laterals at Spanish Trail in Midland County, recently peaked at about 7,500 barrels of oil and 37 million cubic feet of gas per day, above the company’s internal expectations. The company plans full-field Barnett development from 2027.

Diamondback will pay $2.15 billion in cash and about 15.56 million shares for certain subsidiaries of Double Eagle IV Midco and Double Eagle V Midco, the company said. It will fund the cash from cash on hand, its credit facility and term loans. Diamondback values the deal at about four times estimated 2027 EBITDA, expects it to be immediately accretive and leverage neutral, and plans to close on December 21.

The assets cover about 176,000 net acres in the core of the Midland Basin and are expected to produce about 35,000 barrels of oil per day in 2027, out of 92,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. About 68% of the asset is undeveloped, with more than 1,200 gross horizontal locations, 495 of them net, including 101 gross wells drilled but not completed.

The Financial Times reported the talks on Sunday, according to Économie Matin. The purchase follows Diamondback’s $26 billion takeover of Endeavor Energy Resources in 2024 and its $4.08 billion deal for other Double Eagle units last year. Six days ago, Diamondback and KKR agreed to buy Five Point Infrastructure’s 70% stake in Deep Blue, a Midland Basin water network. Double Eagle’s co-CEOs, Cody Campbell and John Sellers, said the company will keep running a multi-rig program on its remaining assets in Reagan County.
